brief_summary: Three horizontal bars drawn to scale (7.874 px per mm) showing Cherry-pattern stabilizer stem spacing: 2u at 23.8mm, 6.25u at 100mm, 7u at 114.3mm. Each bar has stem-housing markers at the ends and a coral-outlined switch square at centre; the 6.25u row carries a coral dimension line for the 50mm moment arm from switch centre to stem. Coral annotation beneath: torsional compliance scales with span, so the 6.25u wire twists about 4.2x as far as the 2u wire under the same torque (100 / 23.8 = 4.2).
data_sources: why-stabilizers-rattle-deep-dive.mdx § 'Why 2u and 6.25u are different keys' — 'Stem spacing on a Cherry-pattern PCB is 23.8mm for 2u keys, 100mm for a 6.25u spacebar, and 114.3mm for a 7u' (https://hilpcb.com/en/blog/keyboard-pcb-layout/)
why-stabilizers-rattle-deep-dive.mdx § 'Why 2u and 6.25u are different keys' — 'the 6.25u wire twists a little over four times as far as the 2u wire under the same torque' (derived: 100 / 23.8 = 4.2)

why-stabilizers-rattle-deep-dive.mdx § 'Why 2u and 6.25u are different keys' — 'On a 2u the stems sit 11.9mm from the switch centre, so the switch carries most of an off-centre press. On a 6.25u the corner is 50mm out'
